affordability.notes: The advertised estimate assumes 20 percent down and excludes renovation risk; the stripped home may not qualify for conventional or USDA financing.

qualification.exceptionReason: The estimated payment is under the target only with roughly $30,000 cash to close, and HOA or deed restrictions remain unverified; the powered pole barn, existing utilities, 2.88 acres, and project-house condition make it worth investigating.
exceptionalStrengths: Large powered pole barn or workshop plus a shed
Existing well, septic, power, and residential dwelling

research.notes: Strong project-property lead, but the payment only works on paper with a down payment Chris and Becky do not currently have. Keep it only if the utilities operate, restrictions are tolerable, and the seller offers a workable acquisition path.

properties.name: 1668 NE 592nd Street
properties.nickname: The Less Scary Old Town Option

affordability.notes: A broker estimate is near the $900 target, but online calculators conflict and the down payment, insurance, taxes, and actual loan terms are unverified.

qualification.exceptionReason: The estimated payment is near the target but real loan terms and cash to close are unverified, with no seller flexibility advertised; two acres, no HOA, a renovated dwelling, and newly replaced core utility components justify keeping it in the Maybe group.
exceptionalStrengths: New well, septic, metal roof, windows, water heater, and appliances
Two acres with no HOA on a paved road
Move-in dwelling within five miles of the Suwannee River

research.notes: The cleaner Becky-facing option. It appears substantially more ready than the project properties, but it does nothing yet to solve the no-overlap purchase problem and must not be treated as affordable until real financing and insurance numbers are obtained.
